senses.definition: A craftsperson who works metal into desired forms using a hammer and other tools, sometimes heating the metal to make it more workable, especially a blacksmith.

quotes.text: The smiths themselves were a grand lot of fellows, full of a robust, and sometimes Rabelaisian sense of humour, and between "heats," they could be most entertaining.
quotes.reference: 1945 January and February, A Former Pupil, “Some Memories of Crewe Works—III”, in Railway Magazine, page 13:

senses.definition: (by extension) One who makes anything; wright.
To forge, to form, usually on an anvil; by heating and pounding.

quotes.text:
Sigurd took the very best sword
That the Dwarfs had ever smithed.
quotes.reference: 1828, Thomas Keightley, The Fairy Mythology, volume I, London: William Harrison Ainsworth, page 258:
